problem: First Sylow theorem: if p is prime and p^n divides the order of a finite group G, then G has a subgroup of order p^n.
proof_idea: Induct on n. The base subgroup is {1}. For the successor step, use Cauchy's theorem in the normalizer quotient to obtain a prime-order quotient subgroup, then take its preimage and the explicit coordinate bijection to enlarge a subgroup of order p^k to one of order p^(k+1).
litex_code:
thm p_power_subgroup_exists:
    ? forall G nonempty_set, group &group::Group<G>, p N+, n N:
        $is_finite_set(G)
        $prime(p)
        $group::divides(p^n, finite_set_size(G))
        =>:
            exist H power_set(G) st {$subgroup::is_subgroup(G, group, H), $is_finite_set(H), finite_set_size(H) = p^n}
